name: FindYourSaaS

sources.title: FindYourSaaS homepage — SaaS directory (3980+ tools, 255+ categories)
Submitmap profile — community gate and flow details
Submitator profile — logo <200KB and 50+ word description rejection rules; nofollow link sampling

conditions: Community gate: the onboard flow reportedly requires three comments and three likes on other people's tools (with live counters) before the listing form unlocks
Standard Listing is $0 only as a 'limited-time offer' against a $15 list price — the free lane is not guaranteed to persist
Free-tier listing links were sampled as nofollow; the $9/month Featured tier is reportedly the only one carrying a backlink
Sign-in is required; the /pricing 'Submit Your Tool' button silently does nothing — navigate directly to /onboard
requirements: SaaS/software tools for a general SaaS directory (3,980+ tools, 255+ categories)
Stated rejection rules: logo must be under 200KB; description must be 50+ words
preparation: Logo under 200KB and a description of 50+ words — both are stated rejection rules
Tool name, URL, card image, category, pricing model, use-case and 'best for' audience tags
Willingness to leave 3 comments and 3 likes on other listings first
workflow: Create an account / sign in (the button opens an auth modal; /sign-in itself is 404)
Go to /pricing and click 'Submit Your Tool' — if the client-side navigation does nothing, open /onboard directly
Clear the community gate (3 comments + 3 likes on other tools)
Fill the listing form: logo, card image, 50+ word description
Submit; third-party reports approval within ~7 days
watchFor: Description under 50 words or logo over 200KB = reported rejection
Free listing links sampled as rel=nofollow — don't count this submission for link equity
$0 price is flagged limited-time; it may revert to $15
The onboard page is fully client-rendered; a text fetch shows only 'Loading…'
countsAsLive: Tool card appears on findyoursaas.com (Recently Listed / its category) with Save/Share/Visit actions
unknowns: First-party confirmation of the comment/like gate and current pricing — pricing page renders client-side only
Whether paid featured upgrades change link follow status
